page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-standard-64 is a general-purpose compute instance equipped with 64 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs and 256 GB of system RAM. Based on a standard 1:4 allocation ratio providing 4.0 GB of memory per core, this configuration offers dedicated CPU capacity for reliable multi-threaded execution without thread contention.

The instance does not bundle local disk storage, meaning persistent storage requires attached network block volumes. It also contains no hardware accelerators or GPUs, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default. Resource cost efficiency is achieved through density, matching high core counts to standard memory footprints without the overhead of specialized accelerator hardware.

Due to its balanced compute-to-memory distribution and high core count, the n4d-standard-64 is tailored for enterprise backend services, container cluster nodes, continuous integration build clusters, and relational database hosting where persistent disk access is handled by remote network volumes.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4d-standard-64 is a general-purpose virtual machine featuring 64 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs and 256 GB of memory, delivering a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance configuration includes zero GPUs and provides no integrated local disk storage, requiring the use of external network-attached volumes for data persistence. Complimentary public IPv4 networking addresses are not included. The server profile prioritizes high core density and balanced memory allocation without the overhead of specialized accelerator hardware. Because of its predictable dedicated core performance and scalable memory pool, the n4d-standard-64 is structured for multi-threaded enterprise services, container orchestration nodes, continuous integration pipelines, batch processing tasks, and mid-tier database management systems.
